rounds.text: Reliable Data Services Ltd is demonstrating exceptional fundamental momentum through its top-line expansion, boasting a median sales growth of 20.9% over the last 10 years [E61] alongside a multi-year sales uptrend [E69], sales up QoQ [E68], and a recent 3% YoY increase [E67]. This sustained commercial vigor underpins a powerful historical earnings compounding engine, evidenced by 10-year compounded profit growth of 16% [E18], accelerating to 23% over 5 years [E19] and maintaining a 16% rate over 3 years [E20]. Furthermore, the business extracts remarkable operational efficiency from its assets, generating a Return on Assets (ROA) of 4.56% that drastically outperforms the sector benchmark of 1.8% [E8]. Conceded: trailing twelve-month profit growth has contracted by -43% [E21] and the dividend yield is nominal at 0.03% [E4]. Nonetheless, the current market capitalization of ₹ 146 Cr [E3] fails to properly credit this structural asset efficiency and decade-long compounding ability.

Reliable Data Services Ltd trades at an elevated trailing P/E of 34.6x based on filed statements [E1], alongside a price-to-book ratio of 3.05x on a price of ₹ 141 against a book value of ₹ 46.3 [E2]. Furthermore, the company commands a P/E of 21.78x against a sector benchmark of 20.02x [E6], indicating that valuation multiples stretch beyond typical sector norms. This premium valuation is entirely disconnected from recent fundamental performance, evidenced by a severe contraction in compounded profit growth over the trailing twelve months down to -43% [E21]. Compounding this deterioration, price growth recently exceeds profit growth by 140%, confirming that market expectations are running aggressively ahead of actual delivery [E56] while official signals flag that earnings growth is decelerating [E72]. The negligible dividend yield of 0.03% [E4] offers virtually no income cushion to investors who are paying these stretched multiples for declining near-term earnings. Conceded: [E18], [E19], [E20], [E61], [E67], [E68], [E69], [E76].

The bear relies heavily on the trailing twelve-month profit contraction [E21] and decelerating earnings [E72], but ignores the powerful multi-year compounding engines that prove this business's structural earning power, namely a 10-year compounded profit growth of 16% [E18], a 5-year rate of 23% [E19], and a 3-year rate of 16% [E20]. The valuation metrics of 34.6x P/E [E1] and 3.05x P/B [E2] are justified by an exceptional Return on Assets of 4.56% that crushes the sector benchmark of 1.8% [E8]. While the bear points to a minor premium over the data provider's sector P/E benchmark [E6], it glosses over the fundamental top-line strength featuring a median sales growth of 20.9% over the last decade [E61], alongside recent positive sales momentum including a 3% YoY increase [E67], a QoQ increase [E68], and a confirmed multi-year sales uptrend [E69]. Conceded: [E4], [E56].

The bull attempts to dismiss the trailing twelve-month profit contraction of -43% [E21] and decelerating earnings [E72] by leaning on historical compounding [E18, E19, E20], but history does not pay dividends or justify a 34.6x P/E [E1] when current momentum has severely broken. The multi-year sales uptrend [E69] and modest 3% YoY sales increase [E67] do not validate a 3.05x price-to-book ratio [E2] or a premium P/E of 21.78x over the sector benchmark of 20.02x [E6], especially when the company's median profit growth of 25.0% [E76] completely leaves the company's actual earnings trajectory behind. Conceded: [E18], [E19], [E20], [E61].
